17 September 2026
Clean Power Hydrogen plc
(“CPH2”, the “Company” or the “Group”)
Issue of Equity
Clean Power Hydrogen plc (AIM: CPH2), the UK-based green hydrogen technology company, announces that 3,216,450 new Ordinary Shares (the “New Ordinary Shares”) in the Company have been issued to in lieu of fees due for advisory services. This issue of New Ordinary Shares allows the Company to deploy its cash resources towards ongoing operations.
Application has been made to the London Stock Exchange for the New Ordinary Shares to be admitted to trading on AIM ("Admission"). Dealings in the New Ordinary Shares are expected to commence on or around 8.00 a.m. on 22 September 2026.
Following Admission, the Company's enlarged issued share capital will comprise 992,845,034 ordinary shares with voting rights in the Company. As the Company holds no shares in treasury, this is the total number of the voting rights in the Company which may be used by shareholders as the denominator for the calculations by which they will determine if they are required to notify their interest, or a change in the interest, in the share capital of the Company under Chapter 5 of the FCA's Disclosure Guidance and Transparency Rules as reflected in the Company's articles of incorporation.

31 July 2026
Clean Power Hydrogen plc
("CPH2", the "Company" or the "Group")
Board Changes
Clean Power Hydrogen plc (AIM: CPH2), the UK-based green hydrogen technology company, announces that, further to the announcement made on 22 June 2026, CPH2 is pleased to announce that the standard regulatory due diligence process has now been completed and, accordingly, Richard Scott's formal appointment as Chief Executive Officer ("CEO") of CPH2 is effective immediately as of today.
Richard Scott joined CPH2 in July 2025 as Chief Commercial Officer and has over 30 years in experience in the energy sector. He has held a number of prominent industry roles having served as Executive Vice President at ACME Greentech, where he led development of its green hydrogen derived fuel business. Prior to this he was Vice President, Global Market Development at World Kinect Corporation (formerly, World Fuel Services) (NYSE: WKC).
As CEO, Richard will lead the Company as
it strategically transitions into a technology development and licensing business.
The Board welcomes Richard to his new role and looks forward to his contribution to delivery of CPH2's new capital-light strategy.
As previously announced, Jonathan Duffy, CEO, and Christopher Train, Non-Executive Chair have agreed to leave the Company with effect from today 31 July 2026.

16 July 2026
Clean Power Hydrogen plc
("CPH2", the "Company" or the "Group")
Result of Conditional Placing and Subscription
Further to the announcement by the Company in respect of the proposed Fundraising dated 1 July 2026 (the "Fundraising Announcement"), Clean Power Hydrogen plc (AIM: CPH2) is pleased to announce that the Company has successfully raised gross proceeds of approximately £7.3 million through:
·
a Firm Placing raising approximately £2.54 million;
·
a Conditional Placing raising approximately £0.61 million;
·
a Conditional Subscription raising approximately £3.65 million;
·
a Directors Subscription of £10,000; and
·
a Retail Offer raising approximately £0.5 million,
in each case at an issue price of 1.5 pence per new Ordinary Share.
The Conditional Placing received additional demand following the Fundraising Announcement and, following discussions between Turner Pope Investments (TPI) Ltd and the Company, has been upscaled to raise a total of £0.61 million.
Consequently,
it is anticipated that, in addition to the already issued 169,333,333 Firm Placing Shares, an additional 40,666,666 Conditional Placing Shares, 243,615,502 Subscription Shares, 666,667 Director Subscription Shares, and 33,333,333 Retail Offer Shares will be issued in relation to the Fundraising, resulting in a total of a further 318,282,168 New Ordinary Shares being issued. The net proceeds from the Fundraising will be used to support the revised strategic direction of the Company, with a focus on transitioning towards a capital-light model, centred on strategic partnerships, manufacturing agreements and the global licensing of its proprietary technology.
The Conditional Placing, Subscription, Directors Subscription and Retail Offer are conditional on, among other things, obtaining approval of the Company's shareholders at the General Meeting of the Company to be held at the offices of K&L Gates LLP, One New Change, London EC4M 9AF at 11:00 a.m. on 20 July 2026 and admission of the Conditional Placing Shares, Subscription Shares, Directors Subscription Shares and Retail Offer Shares to trading on AIM.
Admission and Total Voting Rights
The
169,333,333 Firm Placing Shares were admitted to trading on 7 July 2026 and the net proceeds of the Firm Placing have been received by the Company.
Application has been made for the
Conditional Placing Shares, the Subscription Shares, the Director Subscription Shares and the Retail Offer Shares
to be admitted to trading on AIM. Admission is expected to become effective and dealings in the New Ordinary Shares are expected to commence on or around 8.00 a.m. on 22 July 2026, subject to the approval of the Company's shareholders at the General Meeting.
Following Admission, the Company will have 989,628,584 Ordinary Shares in issue. The Company does not hold any Ordinary Shares in treasury, t
herefore, the total number of voting rights will also be
989,628,584
.
The New Ordinary Shares, including the Firm Placing Shares, will, on Admission, represent approximately 49.27 per cent. of the Enlarged Issued Share Capital and will rank pari passu in all respects with the existing Ordinary Shares, including the right to receive all future dividends and distributions declared, made or paid after the date of Admission.
Other than where defined, capitalised terms used in this announcement have the meanings given to them in the Fundraising Announcement.
Commenting, Richard Scott, Chief Executive Officer, said:
"Our markets continue to grow and CPH2 have developed industry leading and proprietary technology to generate hydrogen at lower cost. The confidence shown by our investors in a new capital light, global licensing model is humbling. We recognise that the innovation journey is always challenging, but our recent setbacks have visible solutions, and our new partners enable international reach. The new leadership team is focused more than ever on delivering for all our stakeholders".

company_30s.what_they_do: Clean Power Hydrogen PLC designs, builds and supplies hydrogen generation, storage and supply solutions for power‑to‑gas, fuel‑cell and industrial markets.
company_30s.why_they_matter: Hydrogen is a cornerstone of the UK’s net‑zero strategy. The company offers modular, low‑emission electrolyser units that can be deployed in commercial and industrial sites, giving it a niche in the fast‑growing green‑fuel market.
company_30s.current_state: The firm is still in the early revenue‑generation phase, relying on equity raises and strategic partnerships to cover cash burn. It has recently appointed new directors and is preparing for a shareholder meeting to discuss funding and future contracts.

rns_narrative: The latest filings show a series of equity issuances and board changes aimed at raising fresh capital. The company has also announced the completion of a conditional subscription and a plan to publish its annual report, signalling an attempt to restore investor confidence.

A second theme is governance and investor communication: the AGM notice, the board changes, and the investor presentation all point to a concerted effort to bring transparency and align with shareholder expectations.

Finally, there is a focus on operational milestones – the company is highlighting a planned restoration to trading and the signing of a term sheet with a hydrogen‑tech partner, which could bring the first commercial contracts.

crowd_tape.bull_narrative: A handful of traders see the equity raise as a sign that the company is finally gaining traction and that a first revenue deal is on the horizon.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Most voices point to continued cash burn, uncertain revenue streams and the risk that the hydrogen market will stay competitive. They worry the company may struggle to turn the new capital into profitable operations.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The chatter has been flat for weeks. The latest posts hint at a possible turning point but overall engagement remains low, leaving room for surprise.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends is flat – no recent spikes, which means a new announcement could trigger a big move.

near_term_catalysts: The AGM and the accompanying investor presentation could reveal a new partnership or a first commercial contract.
Completion of the equity subscription will provide the cash needed to hit production milestones.
A regulatory approval or a government incentive announcement for hydrogen projects could lift sentiment.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a sudden spike in daily volume that coincides with a positive RNS, or a clear statement that the company has secured a first revenue‑generating contract.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock is still deep in the crash phase; we are likely in the early capitulation window. A mean‑reversion bounce will need a clear catalyst – a funding round closing or a signed commercial deal – to confirm that buyers are now interested.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The stock has plunged more than 70 % from its recent peak, which historically gives the best rebounds. If the price climbs to the midpoint of its 52‑week range – roughly double its current level – that’s about a 200 % upside. The deep crash creates a high‑reward, low‑probability play that fits the asymmetric strategy our model rewards.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: If the new capital does not translate into a tangible revenue stream, the company could continue to burn cash and fail to attract institutional buyers. The worst‑case is a further decline to the lowest support level or a delisting if liquidity dries up.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Risk: you could lose up to 80 % of the invested capital if the price stays near its current low. Reward: a 200 % upside if the price recovers to the 52‑week midpoint. The asymmetry is clearly in favour of the long side.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter after a volume spike that confirms the equity raise has closed and the company announces a first commercial contract. Size the position to risk only 2–3 % of your portfolio per trade, set a stop just below the recent low, and target the 52‑week midpoint.
playbook.if_watching: Hold cash until you see a clear announcement of a signed contract or a funding close. Watch the 200‑EMA for a breakout as a confirmation signal.
playbook.if_passing: If the company fails to secure a contract within 3 months or the equity raise collapses, consider exiting to avoid further capital erosion.

ai_insights.bottom_line: Deep crash, silent market, and a potential funding or contract announcement give this hydrogen play a high‑asymmetry upside – a classic contrarian opportunity.
